File-header interpretations are adaptations by FAIR-bioHeaders and are not endorsed by the RDA.

indicators.title: Metadata is identified by a persistent identifier
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: an embedded header has no identity apart from the file that carries it; the file's own identity is assessed under RDA-F1-01D and RDA-F1-02D. A separate metadata record is a repository-level matter.

indicators.title: Data is identified by a persistent identifier
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header states an identifier of this file's own data in a scheme of the pinned identifier-scheme table that is flagged persistent (DOI, versioned INSDC/RefSeq assembly accession, registered CURIE). Names such as GRCh38 are not identifiers, and an accession of the genome that a derived file annotates is credited under RDA-I3-04M, not here.

fair-bioheaders.text: State a persistent identifier of this file's own data, in a registered scheme (see guideline G1).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~identifier: [<persistent identifier of this file, e.g. doi:10.5281/zenodo.6762549>]

gff3-pragma.text: State a persistent identifier of this file's own data, in a registered scheme (see guideline G1).
gff3-pragma.line: #!identifier <persistent identifier of this file, e.g. doi:10.5281/zenodo.6762549>

vcf-meta.text: State a persistent identifier of this file's own data, in a registered scheme (see guideline G1).
vcf-meta.line: ##identifier=<persistent identifier of this file, e.g. doi:10.5281/zenodo.6762549>

indicators.title: Metadata is identified by a globally unique identifier
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: as RDA-F1-01M: the header shares the identity of its file.

indicators.title: Data is identified by a globally unique identifier
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header states a globally unique identifier of this file's data: an identifier in a registered scheme, or a content digest in a defined algorithm (FHR checksum, SeqCol digest). A per-record MD5 in the first FASTA defline is record-level evidence and gives at most partial credit.

indicators.title: Rich metadata is provided to allow discovery
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header carries a fixed set of six discovery elements: subject name, taxon, version, creator, date and an identifier of the data. All six are evidenced; three to five are partial.

indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header contains an identifier of this file's data (identifier, accession, FHR checksum or SeqCol digest) under a key whose meaning is that identifier.

indicators.title: Metadata is offered in such a way that it can be harvested and indexed
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: indexing is done by a searchable resource, not by a file; whether the header can be read by machines is assessed under RDA-I1-01M.

indicators.title: Metadata contains information to enable the user to get access to the data
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header says where the data can be obtained, as a URL. An identifier of the data without a URL is partial.

indicators.title: Metadata can be accessed manually
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: anyone holding the file can read a text header; the route to the metadata is the file distribution.

indicators.title: Data can be accessed manually
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the assessed object is the file itself; how to obtain it again is covered by RDA-A1-01M.

indicators.title: Metadata identifier resolves to a metadata record
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header has no metadata identifier of its own (see RDA-F1-01M).

indicators.title: Data identifier resolves to a digital object
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: with the opt-in online check only, the identifier of this file's data resolves through doi.org or identifiers.org. File contents are never sent.

indicators.title: Data is accessible through an access protocol that supports authentication and authorisation
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: a property of the distribution service, which applies where access must be controlled.

indicators.title: Metadata is guaranteed to remain available after data is no longer available
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: embedded metadata disappears with the file by construction. Deposit the header in a durable record (landing page or archive) as well.

indicators.title: Metadata uses knowledge representation expressed in standardised format
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header lines follow a published header convention that the header declares: a GFF3, VCF or GAF format directive, or a FAIR-bioHeaders schema. Free comment lines are not a standardised representation.

gff3-directive.text: Declare the format and its version on the first line (see guideline G3).

vcf-meta.text: Declare the format and its version on the first line (see guideline G3).

gaf.text: Declare the format and its version on the first line (see guideline G3).
gaf.line: !gaf-version: <GAF version, e.g. 2.2>

fair-bioheaders.text: Add a FAIR-bioHeaders header that names its schema; for a genome, create it with bioheaders combine so that it validates (see guideline G3).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~schema: <schema URL of the FAIR-bioHeaders header type, e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FHR-Specification/main/fhr.json>

indicators.title: Data uses knowledge representation expressed in standardised format
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the data format is a registered standard and is declared in the file (##gff-version, ##fileformat, !gaf-version, or a FAIR-bioHeaders schema). A format recognised only by inspecting the content is not evidence.

indicators.title: Metadata uses machine-understandable knowledge representation
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header declares a machine-readable schema and maps its keys to IRIs (for example with a JSON-LD context). A declared schema without IRI mappings is partial; the shared core has no IRI mappings yet.

fair-bioheaders.text: Map the header keys to IRIs with a JSON-LD context, so that the metadata is machine-understandable (see guideline G3).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~'@context': <URL of a JSON-LD context for the header keys, e.g. https://example.org/context.jsonld>

indicators.title: Data uses machine-understandable knowledge representation
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header gives typed, machine-readable definitions of the data's own fields (VCF INFO and FORMAT lines) or names the vocabulary of the records (GFF3 ##feature-ontology). A declared format without such definitions is partial.

gff3-directive.text: Name the Sequence Ontology release used for feature types (see guideline G4).
gff3-directive.line: ##feature-ontology <URL of the Sequence Ontology release used, e.g. http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/so/2024-11-18/so.owl>

gaf.text: Name the Gene Ontology release used (see guideline G4).
gaf.line: !go-version: <PURL of the GO release used, e.g. http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/go/releases/2026-08-02/go.owl>

fair-bioheaders.text: Point to documentation that defines the fields and vocabularies of the records (see guideline G4).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~documentation: <URL of the documentation of the record fields, e.g. https://example.org/fields.html>

indicators.title: Metadata uses FAIR-compliant vocabularies
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: values backed by a vocabulary are persistent IRIs from registered vocabularies: the taxon as an identifiers.org taxonomy IRI, people as ORCID iDs. A label or a non-persistent web page URL is partial.

gff3-directive.text: Give the taxon as a persistent identifiers.org IRI (see guideline G4).

vcf-meta.text: Give the taxon as a persistent identifiers.org IRI (see guideline G4).

gaf.text: Give the taxon as a persistent identifiers.org IRI (see guideline G4).
gaf.line: !taxon: https://identifiers.org/taxonomy:{value}

fair-bioheaders.text: Give the taxon as a persistent identifiers.org IRI (see guideline G4).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~taxon: {name: <species name, e.g. Caenorhabditis elegans>, uri: https://identifiers.org/taxonomy:{value}}

indicators.title: Data uses FAIR-compliant vocabularies
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header names the vocabularies and versions used in the records (GFF3 ##feature-ontology, GAF !go-version). A format that mandates a vocabulary (GFF3, GAF) without a stated version is partial. Record values are not scanned.

gff3-directive.text: Name the Sequence Ontology release used for feature types (see guideline G4).
gff3-directive.line: ##feature-ontology <URL of the Sequence Ontology release used, e.g. http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/so/2024-11-18/so.owl>

indicators.title: Metadata includes references to other metadata
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header refers to records about related entities by identifier: a taxonomy IRI, an ORCID iD, a DOI of an article. A taxonomy web page URL is partial.

gff3-directive.text: Give the taxon as a persistent identifiers.org IRI (see guideline G4).

vcf-meta.text: Give the taxon as a persistent identifiers.org IRI (see guideline G4).

gaf.text: Give the taxon as a persistent identifiers.org IRI (see guideline G4).

indicators.title: Data includes references to other data
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: cross-references inside the records (GFF3 Dbxref, GAF DB:ID columns, VCF ID). Record bodies are not scanned in this release.

indicators.title: Metadata includes references to other data
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header refers to another dataset: the assembly or reference sequence (checksum, digest, versioned accession or URL), or an ontology release by URL. A name only is partial. Matching sequence names is circumstantial and not credited.

conditions.description: checksum, seqcol, sequence-digests, accession or file URL link
any recorded link, including a name or a directory URL

gff3-pragma.text: Record the accession of the assembly this annotation describes, so that the genome can be identified exactly (see guideline G5).

vcf-meta.text: Give each contig the MD5 of its reference sequence, one line per contig, so that the genome can be checked exactly (see guideline G5).

gaf.text: Name the ontology release the annotations refer to (see guideline G5).
gaf.line: !go-version: <PURL of the GO release used, e.g. http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/go/releases/2026-08-02/go.owl>

fair-bioheaders.text: Add a derivedFrom entry that names the parent file by checksum and states the relationship (see guideline G5).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~derivedFrom: [{headerType: <header type of the parent file, e.g. FHR>, relationship: <relationship to the parent, e.g. annotates>, checksum: {related.checksum}}]

indicators.title: Data includes qualified references to other data
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: qualified links inside the records (GFF3 Parent, Derives_from, Ontology_term). Record bodies are not scanned in this release.

indicators.title: Metadata includes qualified references to other metadata
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: as RDA-I3-01M, and the role of the reference is stated by a key with a published meaning (metadataAuthor, assemblyAuthor, scholarlyArticle).

fair-bioheaders.text: Name the author of the header with an ORCID iD, which states the role and links to a record about the person (see guideline G4).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~metadataAuthor: [{name: <author name, e.g. Josiah Carberry>, uri: https://orcid.org/<ORCID iD, e.g. 0000-0002-1825-0097>}]

indicators.title: Metadata include qualified references to other data
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header refers to the data this file was derived from by an identifier (checksum, SeqCol digest, per-sequence digests, versioned accession, file URL) and states the relationship, either explicitly (derivedFrom) or through a native key whose documented meaning is the relationship (#!genome-build-accession). A name or directory URL alone is partial. Matching sequence names is circumstantial and not credited.

conditions.description: checksum, seqcol, sequence-digests, accession or file URL link
explicit or documented relationship of a recorded link

gff3-pragma.text: Record the accession of the assembly this annotation describes, so that the genome can be identified exactly (see guideline G5).

vcf-meta.text: Give each contig the MD5 of its reference sequence, one line per contig, so that the genome can be checked exactly (see guideline G5).

fair-bioheaders.text: Add a derivedFrom entry that names the parent file by checksum and states the relationship (see guideline G5).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~derivedFrom: [{headerType: <header type of the parent file, e.g. FHR>, relationship: <relationship to the parent, e.g. annotates>, checksum: {related.checksum}}]

indicators.title: Plurality of accurate and relevant attributes are provided to allow reuse
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header carries a fixed list of reuse attributes: version, creator, date, licence, taxon and source data. Accuracy is not judged. All six are evidenced; three to five are partial.

indicators.title: Metadata includes information about the licence under which the data can be reused
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header states a licence under a licence key; human-readable text counts.

indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the licence is an SPDX identifier from the pinned SPDX licence list or the canonical URL of a standard licence. Other licence text is partial.

indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the licence is an SPDX identifier or a standard licence IRI, both of which have machine-readable expressions.

vcf-meta.text: State the licence of this file as an SPDX identifier (see guideline G7).

indicators.title: Metadata includes provenance information according to community-specific standards
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: provenance under keys defined by the convention, in three groups: who (creator or software), when (date) and from what (source annotation or parent data). All three are evidenced; one or two are partial.

gff3-pragma.text: Record when this file was produced (see guideline G6).

vcf-meta.text: Record when this file was produced (see guideline G6).

gaf.text: Record when this file was produced (see guideline G6).
gaf.line: !date-generated: <ISO 8601 date, e.g. 2026-10-10>

fair-bioheaders.text: Record when this file was produced (see guideline G6).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~dateCreated: <ISO 8601 date, e.g. 2026-10-10>

indicators.title: Metadata includes provenance information according to a cross-community language
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: provenance is expressed in, or mapped to, a cross-domain language such as PROV-O. The derivedFrom relationship has no published PROV-O mapping yet (FHR-Specification#54), so it is at most partial; native conventions are not evidenced.

fair-bioheaders.text: Record the parent file with a derivedFrom entry and its relationship; the relationship vocabulary is still provisional (FHR-Specification#54) (see guideline G5).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~derivedFrom: [{headerType: <header type of the parent file, e.g. FHR>, relationship: <relationship to the parent, e.g. annotates>, checksum: {related.checksum}}]

indicators.title: Metadata complies with a community standard
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header meets its convention: a FAIR-bioHeaders header validates against its schema (reported separately as conformance and only cited here); a GFF3, VCF or GAF header declares its format on the first line. A declaration that is not on the first line is partial.

indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the file declares its format and the sampled records (at most --record-limit, reported) parse as that format. Full validation is left to format validators.

gaf.text: Declare the format and its version on the first line (see guideline G3).
gaf.line: !gaf-version: <GAF version, e.g. 2.2>

fair-bioheaders.text: Add a FAIR-bioHeaders header that names its schema; for a genome, create it with bioheaders combine so that it validates (see guideline G3).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~schema: <schema URL of the FAIR-bioHeaders header type, e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FHR-Specification/main/fhr.json>

indicators.title: Metadata is expressed in compliance with a machine-understandable community standard
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the header declares a machine-readable schema and validates against it (FAIR-bioHeaders). GFF3, VCF and GAF headers follow prose specifications only, which is partial.

fair-bioheaders.text: Add a FAIR-bioHeaders header that names its machine-readable schema; for a genome, create it with bioheaders combine so that it validates (see guideline G3).
fair-bioheaders.line: #~schema: <schema URL of the FAIR-bioHeaders header type, e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FHR-Specification/main/fhr.json>

indicators.title: Data is expressed in compliance with a machine-understandable community standard
indicators.interpretation: Adapted: the data format is in the pinned community-format table and is declared in the file with its version (or by a FAIR-bioHeaders schema). A declared format with an unlisted version is partial.
